summary: Search a matrix whose rows and columns are each sorted ascending.
mainInsight: Start at the top-right corner. If the value is greater than the target, no later element in this column can match, so move left; if it is smaller, no earlier element in this row can match, so move down. Each step removes a row or a column, so it needs at most m + n steps.

approaches.name: Staircase search
approaches.summary: Start top-right; move left or down.

approaches.name: Divide and conquer
approaches.summary: Pick the middle and discard a quadrant.

commonMistakes: Mixing up row and column moves
Treating it as the fully sorted matrix (Search a 2D Matrix I)

promptVariants: Where does the staircase search start and why?
Which corner lets you discard a row or a column on every comparison?
options: At the top-right corner: it is the largest in its row and the smallest in its column
At the top-left corner: it is the smallest of the whole matrix
At the centre: it splits the matrix into four sorted quadrants
At the bottom-right corner: it is the largest of the matrix
cards.answer: At the top-right corner: it is the largest in its row and the smallest in its column
cards.explanation: From the top-right, one move direction always decreases and the other always increases.

promptVariants: Why is each comparison guaranteed to eliminate a whole row or column?
What invariant does the staircase maintain?
cards.answer: If the current value is larger than the target, it is the smallest in its column among remaining rows, so everything below it is larger too and the column can be dropped; if smaller, it is the largest in its row among the remaining columns, so everything to the left is smaller and the row can be dropped. The target, if present, always lies in the remaining sub-matrix.
keyPoints: Target stays in the remaining region

cards.explanation: At most one row or column is removed per step.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
What happens if you start at the top-left corner instead?
Why does the algorithm not work from there?
options: Both moves increase the value, so you cannot tell which side to drop
It works the same, only the loop bounds change
It runs in O(log n) because the corner is the minimum
It always misses the last row of the matrix
cards.answer: Both moves increase the value, so you cannot tell which side to drop
cards.explanation: You need one direction that decreases and one that increases.
